Ibn Sa'di's commentary on Surah 78, verses 6–16:

{6–16}: That is, has We not bestowed upon you great blessings? We made {the earth a resting-place} (mihad); that is, spread out and made smooth and pliable for you and for your welfare, for tilling, for dwellings and for roads. {And the mountains as pegs} (awtad): they hold the earth firm so that it does not shake with you and sway. {And We created you in pairs} (azwaj); that is, males and females of a single kind, so that each of them may find tranquility in the other, whereby affection and mercy come into being, and offspring arise from the two of them. Within this favour is also the pleasure of marital union. {And We made your sleep a rest} (subat); that is, a repose for you and a cutting-off of your occupations, which, if they were prolonged, would harm your bodies. So God made the night and sleep cover people, so that their harmful movements may come to rest and their beneficial comfort may be attained. {And We built above you seven strong (heavens)} (shidad); that is, seven heavens in the utmost strength, firmness and solidity, which God holds by His power, and He made them a canopy for the earth, in which there are many benefits for them. For this reason, among their benefits, He mentioned the sun, saying: {And We made a blazing lamp} (siraj wahhaj). By "lamp" He alerted to the blessing of its light, which has become a necessity for creation, and by "wahhaj" (blazing), which means its heat, to what it contains of ripening and benefits. {And We sent down from the rain-clouds} (mu'sirat); that is, the clouds, {abundant water} (ma'an thajjaj); that is, very copious indeed; {that We may bring forth thereby grain} (habban): of wheat, barley, sorghum, rice and other things that human beings eat; {and plants} (nabatan): encompassing all the vegetation that God made as fodder for their livestock; {and gardens of thick growth} (jannat alfafan); that is, orchards intertwined, containing all kinds of delicious fruits. So He who has bestowed upon you these great blessings, whose worth cannot be measured and whose number cannot be counted: how can you disbelieve in Him and deny what He has told you of the resurrection and the rising up? Or how can you use His blessings to disobey Him and deny them?!

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 78, verses 17–30:

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 78, verse 37–40:

{37–39} That is, the One who gave them these gifts is their Lord, {the Lord of the heavens and the earth}: the One who created them and manages them. {The Most Merciful (al-Rahman)}: the One whose mercy encompasses everything, who nurtured them, showed them mercy and was gentle with them until they attained what they attained. Then He mentioned His greatness and His mighty dominion on the Day of Resurrection, and that all creation will be silent on that day, not speaking, and {they will not have the power to address Him}; {except for one whom the Most Merciful permits and who speaks what is right}: no one will speak except under these two conditions: that Allah permits him to speak, and that what he says is right. For {that Day is the Truth (al-Haqq)}: the day on which falsehood finds no market and lying benefits nothing. On that day {the Spirit (al-Ruh)} will stand, and this is Jibril, peace be upon him, who is the most excellent of the angels, {and the angels}, too, will all stand {in rows}, humbled before Allah, speaking only with His permission. When He had encouraged and warned, given glad tidings and given warning, He said: {So whoever wills may take a path to his Lord, a place of return}; that is, a deed and a good standing before Him to which he returns on the Day of Resurrection.

{40} {Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment}: because it has drawn near and approaching, and everything that is coming is near. {On the Day when a man will look at what his hands have put forward}; that is, this is what concerns him and what he will turn to, so let him look in this abode at what he has sent ahead for the abode of permanence. {O you who have believed, fear Allah; and let every soul look to what it has put forward for tomorrow. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do...} (the verses); so if he finds good, let him praise Allah, and if he finds otherwise, let him blame no one but himself. For this reason the disbelievers will wish for death out of the intensity of regret and remorse. We ask Allah to protect us from disbelief and all evil, for He is Generous and Bountiful.

Finished.
